title: Multi-agent Autoformalization of Tensor Network Theory
authors: Sirui Lu, Erickson Tjoa, J. Ignacio Cirac
abstract: We build a team of specialized large language-model agents and present an agent-driven workflow for research-level formalization in theoretical physics, with the autoformalization of the fundamental theorem of matrix-product states as a demonstration. The agents, coordinated through a structured mathematical blueprint and periodic human review, orchestrated and executed the full formalization autonomously. For some statements, the agents were able to explore new proof routes that are not part of the standard literature. Along the way the agents produced extensive tensor-network and quantum-information libraries not previously available in Mathlib, Lean's mathematical library. As a physical application, the formalization also extends towards symmetry-protected topological phases in one dimension. We find that the main bottleneck in large-scale autoformalization is enforcing mathematical intent and we provide a detailed study of the full process and various subtleties involved. We release the codebase as the library \href{https://github.com/LionSR/TNLean}{TNLean}, together with a \nChapters{}-chapter \href{https://lionsr.github.io/TNLean/blueprint/}{blueprint} of the formalization effort.
summary: The paper introduces an agent-driven workflow using specialized LLMs to autoformalize advanced theorems in theoretical physics, demonstrated on Tensor Network Theory. By applying this system to the fundamental theorem of MPS and 1D topological phases, the authors showcase a powerful methodology for machine-checking complex physical mathematics. This effort establishes new computational libraries (TNLean) and highlights that controlling mathematical intent remains the key challenge in scaling such AI formalization efforts.
main_problem: The primary goal is the automated, research-level formalization of complex theorems from theoretical physics, specifically focusing on Tensor Network Theory.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated an agent-driven workflow that autoformalized the fundamental theorem of matrix-product states (FT-MPS) and extended it to classify 1D symmetry-protected topological phases.
method: A multi-agent LLM system coordinates specialized agents using a structured mathematical blueprint, executing formal proofs within the Lean 4 proof assistant for machine verification.
model_or_system: The theory centers on Matrix-Product States (MPS) used to describe quantum states on one-dimensional chains. The formalism connects these states to topological invariants derived from group representations.

important_parameters: The bond dimension ($D$), chain length ($N$), and the nature of the symmetry group $G$ are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: The main bottleneck identified is enforcing correct mathematical intent during autoformalization; furthermore, reliance on primary literature sources was necessary for full autonomy.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate multi-layered consistency checks across literature, blueprints, and Lean code. Another figure shows the flow from FT-MPS to SPT phase classification via a virtual-layer gauge identity.
paper_structure: The paper details the agent workflow (Blueprint $\leftrightarrow$ Lean), presents the formalization of FT-MPS (relating tensors via gauge transformations), extends this to 1D SPT phases, and concludes with a discussion on process limitations and infrastructure release.
why_interesting: This work provides a blueprint for how AI can tackle foundational theoretical physics problems by automating rigorous mathematical proof construction in systems like Lean, which is highly relevant for developing formal quantum field theory or condensed matter models.
